title: grammar anchoring and byte-pair split repair for OpenAI-compat constraint proxy
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes where regex/CFG constraints failed when byte-pair encodings split anchors; adds a constraint proxy in the OpenAI compatibility layer and improved telemetry for constraint failures.
description:
Context and motivation: We have a recurring class of failures where structured-output constraints (regex and CFG backends) silently fail to enforce anchors or prefixes when the tokenizer produces subtokens that split anchor characters or regex prefix spans. This manifests most frequently in OpenAI-compat streaming requests and tool-calling flows where partial tokens are emitted and the constraint backend can't match the intended prefix. Users see non-deterministic allowed outputs, and the streaming shim sometimes emits an early tool call or malformed JSON.

Summary of changes: This PR introduces a small middleware in the OpenAI compatibility layer (constraint proxy) that rewrites high-level constraint directives into token-aware constraints and applies two complementary strategies: (1) grammar anchoring pass that inserts explicit parser anchors when a grammar rule begins with characters commonly split by tokenizers (quotes, braces, punctuation), and (2) byte-pair split repair that detects BPE/subtoken splits across prefix boundaries and synthesizes temporary pseudo-tokens so regex/CFG backends can perform deterministic matching. Additionally: improved unit/integration tests for streaming tool-calling paths, telemetry for constraint mismatch reasons, e2e test for JSON tooling output, and docs updates in the compat README.

Design notes: - Constraint Proxy: sits between the OpenAI compatibility translator and the existing constrained-decoder backends. It inspects the incoming constraint representation (regex/CFG), tokenizes the constraint prefix using the model's tokenizer, and emits a token-mask or augmented grammar that accounts for subtokens. The proxy is intentionally lightweight and reversible.
- Grammar anchoring: when a rule starts with characters like '"', '{', '[', '<', or whitespace-sensitive markers, we synthesize an anchored production that matches across subtoken boundaries rather than byte/character boundaries. This reduces false negatives in grammar enforcement.
- Byte-pair split repair: for regex prefixes, we precompute the shortest token sequence that would produce the prefix string; if the prefix falls inside subtokens, we create an escape-match token that the backend treats as a single logical token.
- Fallback policy: if the proxy detects an ambiguous mapping (multiple plausible tokenizations that alter semantics), it falls back to a conservative acceptance mask and logs the event. This ensures availability at the cost of occasionally looser enforcement; those events are surfaced in telemetry so we can triage high-frequency cases.

Checklist: - [x] Constraint proxy implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests covering streaming + tool call scenarios - [x] End-to-end JSON schema test that previously failed in staged runs - [x] Telemetry events for (a) split-repair applied, (b) fallback-on-ambiguity - [x] Docs/compatibility notes updated - [x] Benchmarked for latency; median increase < 6ms on small prompt sizes

Commits (high-level): - commit 1: "constraint-proxy: initial scaffold, proxy interface and wiring into openai_compat" - commit 2: "grammar-anchor: anchored production generator and tests for common punctuation prefixes" - commit 3: "bpe-repair: compute pseudo-token sequences for split prefixes; add telemetry and fallback logic" - commit 4: "tests: streaming toolcall e2e + JSON schema regression" - commit 5: "docs: compat layer README + changelog entry"

Files changed (high level): - openai_compat/constraint_proxy.py (new): proxy implementation and token-aware rewrites - runtime/decoding/grammar_anchor.py (new): grammar anchoring helpers and tests - runtime/decoding/bpe_repair.py (new): byte-pair split repair utilities - tokenizers/model_bpe.py (updated): new helper to compute minimal token spans - runtime/decoding/constraint_backends/* (updated): small adapters to accept proxy-synthesized pseudo-tokens - tests/compat/test_constraint_proxy_streaming.py (new): integration e2e - docs/compat/constraints.md (updated): guidance for tool authors

Review conversation (highlights): - Aleksandr Ivankov: "This looks promising. Can you add a short microbenchmark to ensure worst-case latency when many prefixes require repair?" - Author (Maya): "Added a small benchmark in tests/perf/test_bpe_repair_latency.py and included results in PR description. Median extra latency ~4.2ms, 95th ~11ms on CI-emulated small instance." - Priya Nair: "What about languages with complex grapheme clusters and right-to-left scripts? Tokenization differences could make anchoring incorrect." - Author: "The proxy uses the model tokenizer for initial segmentation; for grapheme-level cases we detect multi-codepoint clusters and mark them ambiguous to force fallback. I've added test vectors for Arabic/Hebrew and emoji sequences." - Jonah Reyes: "Telemetry fields need a stable schema for downstream billing/alerts." - Author: "Added telemetry schema v1 in observability/telemetry_schemas/constraint_proxy_v1.yaml and emitted events for 'split_repair_applied' and 'constraint_proxy_fallback'."

Requested changes and resolutions: - Add benchmark: added and checked in (resolved). - Add more tests for multilingual cases: added Hebrew/Arabic/emoji vectors (resolved). - Make fallback mode configurable via runtime flag: added runtime config key runtime.constraints.proxy_fallback_mode with options [strict|conservative]; default conservative (resolved).

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (streaming/e2e): initially failed due to flaky streaming framing on CI; root cause was a race in the streaming framing shim when an early toolcall is suppressed by the proxy. Fixed by adding a small yield in the streaming shim and re-run. - lint: pass - safety/scanning: pass - perf/regression: perf test added and within threshold. Final CI status: pass.

Rationale for merging: The fix addresses recurring customer reports where structured constraints appeared to be ignored in production for specific prompts and tool flows. The proxy provides a safer mapping between character-level constraints and token-driven backends without changing the backend APIs. Telemetry ensures we can identify future hotspots and tune heuristics.

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-18 by Maya Chen. Notes: documented changelog under release_notes and added a short deprecation note for legacy constraint hints that bypass token-aware mapping.

Follow-ups: - ENG-9245: Add server-side opt-in toggle for stricter enforcement mode in enterprise Dedicated installs. - ENG-9252: Gather top 100 fallback events in telemetry and build targeted grammar rules for frequent cases. - Docs: add example showing how to author token-friendly regex constraints for OpenAI compat layer.
